_comment: Phase 2F.4 hardware-assisted validation gate configuration. Consumed by tools/phase2f_hardware_gate.ps1. Docs/tooling artifact - not firmware source. Superset of tools/phase2e_hardware_gate_config.json (which remains frozen/untouched for the accepted Phase 2E-only baseline) - covers all 19 apps (16 Phase 2A/2B/2C/2D/2E + 3 Phase 2F: qrcode, hex_viewer, barcode_gen) now in the accepted Phase 2F baseline. fcc_id_lookup is not part of this baseline - it remains deferred pending a license-evidence resolution and is intentionally absent from allowedApps below. image_viewer's example_images/ (including spongebob.bm, dolphin.bm, cat.bm) remains excluded and is not referenced here as an expected asset.

acceptedBaseline.note: This is the exact commit and CI evidence the Phase 2F acceptance record (docs/PHASE2F_3_ACCEPTANCE_RECORD.md) and artifact hash manifest (docs/PHASE2F_3_ARTIFACT_HASHES.md) cover. Hardware-assisted validation against a different commit is not itself wrong, but should be flagged for review rather than silently treated as validating this same accepted baseline.

phase2F2ARemediationNotes.ciToolingFix: tools/phase2a_validate.ps1 was narrowly fixed (commit 8e5f78f) so native stderr output from the updater_package external-process invocation no longer becomes a misleading terminating PowerShell exception under $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' - the fix scopes $ErrorActionPreference to 'Continue' around just that one cmd /c call, relying on $LASTEXITCODE as the authoritative pass/fail signal. This gate does not re-verify that fix directly (it is a CI-only script behavior, not something observable from a hardware gate), but records it here for full remediation-history traceability.
phase2F2ARemediationNotes.barcodeGenSourceFix: applications_user/barcode_gen/views/create_view.c had 5 dead calls to text_input_show_illegal_symbols() removed (commit b6445ed) - a function belonging only to an unwired, never-integrated custom keyboard fork bundled in the app (keyboard/text_input.c/.h). The app's real text_input widget is a system TextInput instance with no such function and a different internal model layout. This was a user-approved fix after direct evidence was presented via AskUserQuestion. No other logic, control flow, or behavior changed in that file. This gate performs a Preflight-level source-content check confirming this fix remains preserved (i.e. text_input_show_illegal_symbols is NOT present in create_view.c) - a regression here (the dead calls reappearing) would indicate the file was reverted or overwritten and must be investigated before any hardware-connected step proceeds.

expectedArtifacts.note: These are the real, GitHub-Actions-generated values recorded in docs/PHASE2F_3_ARTIFACT_HASHES.md (Phase 2F.3, finalization run 29027115867) - not fabricated, not archive-level digests. HashVerify/HardwareAssisted modes compare a locally-downloaded artifact directory's actual files against these exact values.

expectedFapNamesNote: All 19 filenames are the manifest-declared appid-based .fap output names, confirmed present in the accepted CI run's job log and independently re-hashed by the finalization workflow (docs/PHASE2F_3_ARTIFACT_HASHES.md). qrcode.fap, hex_viewer.fap, and barcode_app.fap are the 3 Phase 2F apps specifically. These are informational only in this gate - this script does not itself build or inspect .fap files, since no Windows/fbt build is performed here.
expectedAppPrivateStoragePathsNote: null means the app is not expected to persist any file under normal use; any storage write by these apps outside their own entry (or any write at all, for the null-path apps) is a fail condition per the hardware smoke-test checklist. All notes for the 16 already-accepted apps are unchanged, carried forward from tools/phase2e_hardware_gate_config.json. qrcode, hex_viewer, and barcode_gen (new in Phase 2F) are covered by dedicated notes below, matching the direct source-level findings in docs/PHASE2F_2_SAFETY_REVIEW.md and docs/PHASE2F_2_LICENSE_ATTRIBUTION.md.
sdInfoStorageNote: sd_info is NOT zero-storage and NOT app-private, per the real source read in Phase 2C.1/2C.2: its SD-card speed test writes, reads back, and deletes benchmark blocks at /ext/sdtest.tmp* (SD-card root, TEST_FILE_PATH = "/ext/sdtest.tmp"), 48 write/read/verify/delete cycles of 32KB blocks, ONLY when the user explicitly presses OK to start the test on the app's own test page. This is controlled, self-cleaning, and transient - not persistent, not automatic, not a safety-exclusion-list capability - but it is a real write to the SD-card root, materially different from an app-private save file or a read-only app. The hardware smoke-test checklist must confirm no /ext/sdtest.tmp* files remain after a normal test completion or after aborting mid-test.
docviewliteStorageNote: docviewlite is confirmed read-only by source: it opens and reads a user-selected .txt file via the standard Flipper file-browser dialog and storage_file_read only - no storage_file_write call exists anywhere in its source. The hardware smoke-test checklist should confirm no new file or modification appears anywhere on the SD card after using this app.
resistorsStorageNote: resistors is confirmed zero-storage by source: no `storage_`, `file_stream`, `RECORD_STORAGE`, `FSAM_`, or `FSOM_` reference anywhere in its source, and zero `furi_hal` usage of any kind. The hardware smoke-test checklist should confirm no file of any kind appears on the SD card after using this app.
cryptoDictionaryStorageNote: crypto_dictionary is confirmed read-only by source: it opens its own bundled glossary .txt files via FSAM_READ/FSOM_OPEN_EXISTING only - no write call anywhere in its source, and zero furi_hal usage. The hardware smoke-test checklist should confirm no new file or modification appears anywhere on the SD card after using this app, including after searching/browsing the bundled glossary.
game2048StorageNote: 2048 is confirmed to write only to its own app-scoped save file, per direct source read: /ext/apps_data/game_2048/game_2048.save via a hardcoded EXT_PATH("apps_data/game_2048") literal. It also performs a one-time legacy-path migration check against /ext/apps/Games/game_2048.save on load, which is a silent no-op on this baseline (no such file exists) and should not be observed to write anywhere outside /ext/apps_data/game_2048/. The hardware smoke-test checklist should confirm the only file written during play is game_2048.save under that directory.
imageViewerStorageNote: image_viewer is confirmed read-only by source: it opens whatever file the user selects via the standard Flipper file-browser dialog with FSAM_READ only - no storage_file_write call anywhere in its source. The bundled example_images/ directory (cat.bm, dolphin.bm, and spongebob.bm - the latter confirmed to depict a recognizable trademarked/copyrighted cartoon character with no attribution or redistribution-rights evidence) was excluded at import and remains absent from applications_user/image_viewer/ - this app's own behavior does not depend on it, since it opens whatever the user selects, not a hardcoded bundled filename. The hardware smoke-test checklist must confirm no new file or modification appears anywhere on the SD card after using this app, and must confirm example_images/ is not present in the imported app directory before testing.
boilerplateStorageNote: boilerplate is confirmed app-private by source: it writes its own configuration file to /ext/apps_data/boilerplate/boilerplate.conf. The hardware smoke-test checklist should confirm any write by this app is confined to /ext/apps_data/boilerplate/ and nowhere else on the SD card.
minesweeperStorageNote: minesweeper is confirmed app-private by source: it writes save/config state to /ext/apps_data/mine_sweeper_redux/ via an atomic write-then-rename pattern. The hardware smoke-test checklist should confirm any write by this app is confined to /ext/apps_data/mine_sweeper_redux/ and nowhere else on the SD card, and that no partial/temp file from an interrupted write survives outside that directory.
qrcodeStorageNote: qrcode is confirmed read-only for QR content by source, per docs/PHASE2F_2_SAFETY_REVIEW.md: qrcode_load_file() uses flipper_format_read_* calls exclusively - no write function exists in this version of the app for QR content itself. One real, bounded, benign storage-write pattern exists: a one-time legacy-folder migration at every launch (storage_common_copy(ANY_PATH("qrcodes"), QRCODE_FOLDER) followed by storage_common_remove(ANY_PATH("qrcodes"))), the same class of migration already accepted for 2048. The hardware smoke-test checklist should confirm this migration (if it occurs at all - only relevant if a legacy /ext/qrcodes/ folder exists) completes cleanly and no other write occurs anywhere on the SD card while displaying/generating QR codes.
hexViewerStorageNote: hex_viewer is confirmed genuinely read-only for viewed files by source, per docs/PHASE2F_2_SAFETY_REVIEW.md: files are opened with FSAM_READ/FSOM_OPEN_EXISTING only - no write, edit, patch, overwrite, or delete call touches the viewed file anywhere in the source. Its own settings (4 boolean toggles: haptic/speaker/LED/save-settings) are app-private at /ext/apps_data/hex_viewer/. The hardware smoke-test checklist should confirm the viewed file is never modified, and that any settings write is confined to /ext/apps_data/hex_viewer/.
barcodeGenStorageNote: barcode_gen (real appid barcode_app) is confirmed app-private by source, per docs/PHASE2F_2_SAFETY_REVIEW.md: all create/edit/rename/delete operations (storage_simply_mkdir, storage_common_rename, storage_simply_remove) are confined to /ext/apps_data/barcodes/ (DEFAULT_USER_BARCODES). No scanner-emulation, access-control, HID, NFC, or USB behavior of any kind. The hardware smoke-test checklist should confirm any write by this app is confined to /ext/apps_data/barcodes/ and nowhere else on the SD card, and that the app performs local barcode display/generation only - no radio/RF/hardware-peripheral interaction.
excludedAssetsNote: applications_user/image_viewer/example_images/ (3 bundled .bm demo images: cat.bm, dolphin.bm, spongebob.bm) remains excluded from the accepted Phase 2F baseline and must not be reintroduced by this gate, any script it invokes, or any hardware test performed against docs/PHASE2F_HARDWARE_SMOKE_TEST_CHECKLIST.md. spongebob.bm specifically was confirmed to depict a recognizable trademarked/copyrighted cartoon character with no attribution or redistribution-rights evidence anywhere in the app. This script performs a directory-absence check for applications_user/image_viewer/example_images/ as part of its Preflight/automated checks.
barcodeGenSourceFixNote: applications_user/barcode_gen/views/create_view.c must NOT contain any call to text_input_show_illegal_symbols - that function belongs only to this app's own unwired, never-integrated custom keyboard fork (keyboard/text_input.c/.h) and was removed (5 dead call sites, commit b6445ed, user-approved) because the app's real text_input widget is a system TextInput instance with a different, incompatible internal model layout. This script performs a Preflight-level source-content check confirming this fix remains preserved.
forbiddenTestCategories: Any cloning, brute force, jamming, deauth, or bypass behavior
forbiddenTestCategoriesNote: This script contains no code path for any of the above, for any app, under any flag or mode - this is not a configuration toggle to disable, it is simply not implemented anywhere in tools/phase2f_hardware_gate.ps1.
flashConfirmationPhrase: I UNDERSTAND THIS WILL FLASH THE CONNECTED DEVICE
flashConfirmationNote: The script never performs a flash itself under any circumstance - even after -AllowFlashPrompt and a correctly-typed confirmation phrase, flashing remains a manual, deliberate action performed by the operator using qFlipper or fbt flash_usb outside this script. The confirmation gate exists to make sure the operator has seen the artifact hashes and rollback warning before proceeding, not to automate the flash itself.

deviceDetection.note: Flipper Zero enumerates as a USB CDC-ACM serial device (ST Microelectronics VID 0483, PID 5740) when running normal firmware. Detection uses Windows PnP device enumeration (Get-PnpDevice) only - no serial communication, no RPC, no data exchange with the device.

officialToolingDetection.note: Best-effort detection only (PATH lookup, common install directories, and the Windows uninstall registry key). Absence of a detected install does not necessarily mean qFlipper isn't present under a nonstandard path - it means this script could not confirm it automatically, and flashing tooling should be classified BLOCKED / TOOLING NOT AVAILABLE rather than assumed present.

reportFilenameCollisionFix: Phase 2A's and Phase 2B's hardware gate scripts used second-granularity report filenames (yyyyMMdd_HHmmss), so two invocations within the same wall-clock second could silently overwrite each other's report - a real, documented, minor tooling limitation. tools/phase2c_hardware_gate.ps1 fixed this using a millisecond-precision timestamp plus a short random hex suffix (yyyyMMdd_HHmmss_fff_XXXX) - collision-resistant even for rapid repeated invocations. tools/phase2d_hardware_gate.ps1, tools/phase2e_hardware_gate.ps1, and this script preserve this exact fix unchanged. Phase 2A's and Phase 2B's own scripts are deliberately left unmodified, per this project's standing instruction not to touch them.
